## 8. Weapons and items

### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Electric grenade** (throwable).

### Melee
- **No melee before the elemental sword** (§11).

### Consumables
| Item | Era | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Health potion | Past | Heals a set amount **over time** |
| Mana potion | Past | Restores a set amount of mana **over time** |
| Electric grenade | Future | Throwable, electric damage |
| Health injection | Future | Heals **instantly**, but less than the potion |

### Synergies
Weapon mechanics and spell mechanics combine. The weapon enchant (§6) is the first confirmed one. Other synergies (e.g. shooting through a fire wall, electric grenade on an ice floor) are **TBD**.

## 9. Controls

| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|
| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | **TBD** |
| Aim (gun) | Right click | **TBD** |
| Spell slot 1 | Right click | L1 / LB |
| Spell slots 2–5 | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
| Weapon enchant, jump, dash, switch weapon, grenade, consumables, inventory, skill tree | **TBD** | **TBD** |

- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
- **The true final boss.**
- Enemy types per era and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).

## 11. Bosses and endgame
**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**

Rewards:
| Defeated in | Drops |
|---|---|
| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |
| Future | **A weapon hilt** |
| Both fights | One **quest item** each (what they are: **TBD**) |

- **Elemental sword:** in the inventory, the player combines the hilt with a gem and gets an elemental sword that comes out of the hilt. The player can switch the sword to the other elements from the inventory. It is the only melee weapon. The weapon enchant does not apply to it.
- **Final portal:** combining the two quest items opens a portal to a separate map, a dimension between space and time, where the player fights the **true final boss** (**TBD**).
- This happens in mid/late game.

## 12. Inventory
Needed for: consumables, equipping/unequipping spells, choosing the enchant element, combining hilt + gem, switching the sword's element, combining the two quest items. Layout and limits **TBD**.

## 13. UI: two styles
The UI changes with what the player holds:

| Holding | HUD style |
|---|---|
| Staff (magic) | **1990s first-person RPG** |
| Gun | **Modern cyberpunk** |

Our reading (owner, 2026-11-12): the theme is effectively **open**; what the organizers ask for is a game with an **author's signature**, a personal vision. We answer it with the game's own identity:

| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
| Weapon enchant, jump, dash, switch weapon, grenade, consumables, inventory, skill tree | **TBD** | **TBD** |

Note: right click is both "spell slot 1" and "aim". See open question 2.

## 10. Enemies and encounters
- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
- **The true final boss.**
- Enemy types per era and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).

## 11. Bosses and endgame
**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**

Rewards:
| Defeated in | Drops |
|---|---|
| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |
| Future | **A weapon hilt** |
| Both fights | One **quest item** each (what they are: **TBD**) |

- **Elemental sword:** in the inventory, the player combines the hilt with a gem and gets an elemental sword that comes out of the hilt. The player can switch the sword to the other elements from the inventory. It is the only melee weapon. The weapon enchant does not apply to it.
- **Final portal:** combining the two quest items opens a portal to a separate map, a dimension between space and time, where the player fights the **true final boss** (**TBD**).
- This happens in mid/late game.

## 12. Inventory
Needed for: consumables, equipping/unequipping spells, choosing the enchant element, combining hilt + gem, switching the sword's element, combining the two quest items. Layout and limits **TBD**.

## 13. UI: two styles
The UI changes with what the player holds:

| Holding | HUD style |
|---|---|
| Staff (magic) | **1990s first-person RPG** |
| Gun | **Modern cyberpunk** |
| Elemental sword | **TBD** |

- **Skill trees** follow the same split: the spell tree has its own 90s-RPG look, the weapon tree its own cyberpunk look.
- The HUD switches when the player switches weapon. The inventory's look is **TBD**.

## 14. Theme fit (DIRECTOR'S CUT)
Our reading (owner, 2026-11-12): the theme is effectively **open**; what the organizers ask for is a game with an **author's signature**, a personal vision. We answer it with the game's own identity:
- the hard art split (pixel-art magic vs. 3D cyberpunk) that follows each object and never breaks, with a pixel-art mage holding 3D guns;
- a UI that also changes style with what the player holds;
- magic that has to be performed (the QTE) rather than triggered;
- a combat style that rewards mixing the two eras.

The dev log shows the directing side too: how we direct the AI agents, and every scope decision ("what made the final cut"). Any feature we drop gets logged as a cut, with the reason.

## 15. Scope for the jam (proposal, to discuss)
The jam is 4 days and we package a playable build every day. Suggested order so that every day ends with something playable:

| Day | Target |
|---|---|
| 1 (Nov 12) | First-person controller (move, dash, double jump), pixel-art hands, one staff, one gun, one spell with data-driven parameters, mana/health, one portal swapping eras in a test map. Packaged. |
| 2 (Nov 13) | Rest of guns + spells, 5-slot loadout, weapon enchant, both HUD styles, basic enemies and one wave, consumables, QTE first version. |
| 3 (Nov 14) | Sub-bosses, Valkyrie fights, inventory + elemental sword, skill trees, era-gated zones. |
| 4 (Nov 15) | Final boss arena, polish, audio, video, submission (deadline 20:59 EST). |

- Player controller: movement, double jump, dash, speed modifiers (air passives).

- 5-slot spell loadout + the fixed enchant slot; equip/unequip.
- Spell QTE: input sequence (KB/M and gamepad), gesture recognition (mouse and right stick), per-step grading, global time dilation as a configurable, gear-modifiable value; can be disabled.

- Spawned spell actors: walls, floor zone, ground trap, moving damage ball, sustained flamethrower.
- Era system: same map in two times, portals, era-gated zones, past actions that open future zones, player state kept across eras.
- **Rendering of the art rule per object:** pixel-art sprites (player hands, medieval props, enemies, spells) and 3D meshes (guns, cyberpunk world) in the same first-person view.
- Two UI skins (90s RPG, modern cyberpunk) for HUD and skill trees, switched by the held item.
- Encounters: waves, sub-bosses, bosses (free + fight + drops), skill point rewards.
- Inventory with item combining; two skill trees.
- Final portal and separate final-boss map.
- Input for keyboard & mouse and gamepad (layout in §9).

## 17. Open questions
Answers get folded into the sections above as they come.

**Blocking (needed before the architect starts):**
1. **Weapon skill tree:** what does it upgrade (damage, fire rate, magazine, reload, the enchant)? Before, the skill tree only upgraded spells.
2. **Right click with a gun:** right click is spell slot 1 and also aim. With a gun in hand, is slot 1 lost, or does it move to another key? Same on gamepad: L1 is slot 1, so which button aims and which shoots (R2 / RT for shooting?).
3. **Switching between staff and gun:** how many weapons does the player carry at once, and how do they switch (mouse wheel, a key, a weapon wheel)?
4. **The enchant's key:** it is outside the 5 slots, so which key / button casts it?

**Can wait:**
5. **Elemental sword art:** the hilt is from the future (3D) and the blade is magic (pixel art?). And which HUD does it use?
6. **Staffs:** how many, what each basic attack does, where they are found.
7. **Valkyries and the final boss:** pixel art in the past and 3D in the future? What style is the final boss in the dimension between eras?
8. How "combining styles" is rewarded beyond synergies (combo meter, bonus damage, more skill points?).
9. Do the ice shield and the air passives use the QTE? Do air passives take a slot of the 5?
10. Gun ammo: does it exist, and where does it come from?
11. Sub-bosses: how many, which era, what they are.
12. Examples of era-gated zones and past→future unlocks.
13. Enemy types per era.
14. The two quest items and the true final boss.
15. QTE: time limit, sequence length per spell, does the camera slow too.
16. Armor/gear system: in scope, or only the time-slow modifier?
17. Game and team name.

## 4. World and travel
- **One map, two times** (past and future). The player travels between them **only through predefined portals** placed on the map.
- **Era-gated zones:** some zones are reachable in one era and not in the other.
- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).

## 5. Player progression
- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
- Progression is through **skill trees**: one for spells and one for weapons (see §13 for their look). What the weapon tree upgrades is **TBD** (open question 1).
- **Skill points** are given at specific points, mainly for defeating enemies:
  - defeating each **sub-boss**;
  - defeating each **boss**;
  - **clearing a wave** of enemies.

## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.

| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS) |
| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
| **Ice** | Ice shield (held block, like a first-person RPG shield, but with a cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |

### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- Keys: see §9.

### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.

### General
- Spells cost **mana**.
- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.

## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).

Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.

### Flow
1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
   - Gamepad: the right stick.
4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.

### Grading and cost
- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.

### What each part scales
| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
|---|---|---|
| Fireball | Damage | Blast radius / range |
| Ice wall | Duration and wall health | Width and height |
| Others | **TBD**, following the same idea: part 1 = strength, part 2 = size/area/range |

### Requirements for the architect
- **Every spell parameter is data, not code**, and every one can be tagged as scaled by part 1, part 2, or neither. Each spell defines its own min/max per parameter.
- The **time-slow amount is configurable** and can be modified by gear (e.g. some armor). Armor/gear as a system is otherwise **TBD**.

## 8. Weapons and items

### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
- Staff list and how they are found: **TBD**.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Electric grenade** (throwable).

### Melee
- **No melee before the elemental sword** (§11).

### Consumables
| Item | Era | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Health potion | Past | Heals a set amount **over time** |
| Mana potion | Past | Restores a set amount of mana **over time** |
| Electric grenade | Future | Throwable, electric damage |
| Health injection | Future | Heals **instantly**, but less than the potion |

### Synergies
Weapon mechanics and spell mechanics combine. The weapon enchant (§6) is the first confirmed one. Other synergies (e.g. shooting through a fire wall, electric grenade on an ice floor) are **TBD**.

## 9. Controls

| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |
|---|---|---|
| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | **TBD** |
| Aim (gun) | Right click | **TBD** |
| Spell slot 1 | Right click | L1 / LB |
| Spell slots 2–5 | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
| Weapon enchant, jump, dash, switch weapon, grenade, consumables, inventory, skill tree | **TBD** | **TBD** |

Note: right click is both "spell slot 1" and "aim". See open question 2.

## 10. Enemies and encounters
- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
- **The true final boss.**
- Enemy types per era and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).

## 11. Bosses and endgame
**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**

Rewards:
| Defeated in | Drops |
|---|---|
| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |
| Future | **A weapon hilt** |
| Both fights | One **quest item** each (what they are: **TBD**) |

- **Elemental sword:** in the inventory, the player combines the hilt with a gem and gets an elemental sword that comes out of the hilt. The player can switch the sword to the other elements from the inventory. It is the only melee weapon. The weapon enchant does not apply to it.
- **Final portal:** combining the two quest items opens a portal to a separate map, a dimension between space and time, where the player fights the **true final boss** (**TBD**).
- This happens in mid/late game.

## 12. Inventory
Needed for: consumables, equipping/unequipping spells, choosing the enchant element, combining hilt + gem, switching the sword's element, combining the two quest items. Layout and limits **TBD**.

## 13. UI: two styles
The UI changes with what the player holds:

| Holding | HUD style |
|---|---|
| Staff (magic) | **1990s first-person RPG** |
| Gun | **Modern cyberpunk** |
| Elemental sword | **TBD** |

- **Skill trees** follow the same split: the spell tree has its own 90s-RPG look, the weapon tree its own cyberpunk look.
- The HUD switches when the player switches weapon. The inventory's look is **TBD**.

## 14. Theme fit (DIRECTOR'S CUT)
Our reading (owner, 2026-11-12): the theme is effectively **open**; what the organizers ask for is a game with an **author's signature**, a personal vision. We answer it with the game's own identity:
- the hard art split (pixel-art magic vs. 3D cyberpunk) that follows each object and never breaks, with a pixel-art mage holding 3D guns;
- a UI that also changes style with what the player holds;
- magic that has to be performed (the QTE) rather than triggered;
- a combat style that rewards mixing the two eras.

The dev log shows the directing side too: how we direct the AI agents, and every scope decision ("what made the final cut"). Any feature we drop gets logged as a cut, with the reason.

## 15. Scope for the jam (proposal, to discuss)
The jam is 4 days and we package a playable build every day. Suggested order so that every day ends with something playable:

| Day | Target |
|---|---|
| 1 (Nov 12) | First-person controller (move, dash, double jump), pixel-art hands, one staff, one gun, one spell with data-driven parameters, mana/health, one portal swapping eras in a test map. Packaged. |
| 2 (Nov 13) | Rest of guns + spells, 5-slot loadout, weapon enchant, both HUD styles, basic enemies and one wave, consumables, QTE first version. |
| 3 (Nov 14) | Sub-bosses, Valkyrie fights, inventory + elemental sword, skill trees, era-gated zones. |
| 4 (Nov 15) | Final boss arena, polish, audio, video, submission (deadline 20:59 EST). |

## 16. For the architect: systems to design
Not decisions, just the list of systems the design implies:
- Player controller: movement, double jump, dash, speed modifiers (air passives).
- Health, mana, damage, status effects (slow, heal/mana over time, instant heal, temporary weapon buff).
- Ability system shared by spells, staff attacks, guns and grenade (cooldowns, costs, upgrades from the skill trees). Unreal's Gameplay Ability System is one candidate; the architect decides.
- **Data-driven spell definitions:** every parameter configurable, with min/max and a tag saying whether QTE part 1 (power) or part 2 (reach) scales it.
- 5-slot spell loadout + the fixed enchant slot; equip/unequip.
- Spell QTE: input sequence (KB/M and gamepad), gesture recognition (mouse and right stick), per-step grading, global time dilation as a configurable, gear-modifiable value; can be disabled.
- Held items: staffs (basic attack per staff), guns (shoot, aim), electric grenade, enchant buff, melee sword with swappable element.
- Spawned spell actors: walls, floor zone, ground trap, moving damage ball, sustained flamethrower.
- Era system: same map in two times, portals, era-gated zones, past actions that open future zones, player state kept across eras.
- **Rendering of the art rule per object:** pixel-art sprites (player hands, medieval props, enemies, spells) and 3D meshes (guns, cyberpunk world) in the same first-person view.
- Two UI skins (90s RPG, modern cyberpunk) for HUD and skill trees, switched by the held item.
- Encounters: waves, sub-bosses, bosses (free + fight + drops), skill point rewards.
- Inventory with item combining; two skill trees.
- Final portal and separate final-boss map.
- Input for keyboard & mouse and gamepad (layout in §9).

## 17. Open questions
Answers get folded into the sections above as they come.

**Blocking (needed before the architect starts):**
1. **Weapon skill tree:** what does it upgrade (damage, fire rate, magazine, reload, the enchant)? Before, the skill tree only upgraded spells.
2. **Right click with a gun:** right click is spell slot 1 and also aim. With a gun in hand, is slot 1 lost, or does it move to another key? Same on gamepad: L1 is slot 1, so which button aims and which shoots (R2 / RT for shooting?).
3. **Switching between staff and gun:** how many weapons does the player carry at once, and how do they switch (mouse wheel, a key, a weapon wheel)?
4. **The enchant's key:** it is outside the 5 slots, so which key / button casts it?

**Can wait:**
5. **Elemental sword art:** the hilt is from the future (3D) and the blade is magic (pixel art?). And which HUD does it use?
6. **Staffs:** how many, what each basic attack does, where they are found.
7. **Valkyries and the final boss:** pixel art in the past and 3D in the future? What style is the final boss in the dimension between eras?
8. How "combining styles" is rewarded beyond synergies (combo meter, bonus damage, more skill points?).
9. Do the ice shield and the air passives use the QTE? Do air passives take a slot of the 5?
10. Gun ammo: does it exist, and where does it come from?
11. Sub-bosses: how many, which era, what they are.
12. Examples of era-gated zones and past→future unlocks.
13. Enemy types per era.
14. The two quest items and the true final boss.
15. QTE: time limit, sequence length per spell, does the camera slow too.
16. Armor/gear system: in scope, or only the time-slow modifier?
17. Game and team name.

content.text:
Actualicé [Design/GDD.md](Design/GDD.md) a la **v0.3** y lo commiteé (`9a5472f`).

**Qué incorporé:**
- **Regla de arte por objeto:** una pistola 3D sigue en 3D en el pasado y una bola de fuego sigue en pixel art en el futuro. El jugador es un mago medieval, así que siempre es pixel art, manos incluidas, aunque sostenga un arma 3D. Lo añadí al tema como parte del sello de autor: un mago pixel art que empuña armas 3D.
- **5 hechizos equipados**, que se equipan y desequipan. Hay una tabla de controles nueva (§9) con clic derecho y 1–4, y en mando L1 o L2 más los botones frontales.
- **Bastones:** con el clic primario hacen un ataque mágico básico que depende del bastón. **Armas:** clic primario dispara y secundario apunta.
- **Encantamiento:** tiene QTE, el jugador elige el elemento al equiparlo y no funciona sobre la espada.
- **QTE:** el hechizo se lanza si el jugador acierta al menos un paso, solo falla si los falla todos, y el maná se gasta siempre.
- **Dos estilos de UI:** HUD de RPG de los 90 con bastón y HUD cyberpunk moderno con arma. Cada árbol de habilidades tiene su propia estética.

**Preguntas que bloquean al arquitecto:**
1. **Árbol de armas:** antes solo había árbol de hechizos. ¿Qué mejora el de armas: daño, cadencia, cargador, recarga, el encantamiento?
2. **Choque en el clic derecho:** el clic derecho es el hechizo 1 y también apuntar. Con un arma en la mano, ¿se pierde el hechizo 1 o pasa a otra tecla? En mando pasa lo mismo con L1: ¿con qué botón se apunta y con cuál se dispara (¿R2?)?
3. **Cambio de arma:** ¿cuántas armas lleva el jugador a la vez y cómo cambia entre bastón y pistola: rueda del mouse, una tecla o una rueda de armas?
4. **Tecla del encantamiento:** está fuera de los 5 hechizos, ¿con qué tecla o botón se lanza?

**Pueden esperar, pero son útiles:**
5. **Espada elemental:** el mango es del futuro (3D) y la hoja es mágica. ¿La hoja va en pixel art? ¿Qué HUD usa la espada?
6. **Valquirias y boss final:** ¿pixel art en el pasado y 3D en el futuro? ¿En qué estilo va el boss de la dimensión entre épocas?
7. **Pasivas de aire:** ¿ocupan una de las 5 ranuras o están siempre activas? ¿El escudo de hielo, que se sostiene, también tiene QTE?
8. **Bastones:** ¿cuántos hay y dónde se consiguen?

El resto sigue en la sección 17 del documento: munición, subjefes, zonas bloqueadas, enemigos, objetos de misión, armaduras y nombre del juego.

content.text:
Actualicé [Design/GDD.md](Design/GDD.md) a la **v0.4** y lo commiteé (`066fe1c`).

**Qué incorporé:**
- **Árbol de armas:** daño, cadencia, retroceso, daño según la distancia (la escopeta pega más de cerca y el fusil de lejos) y daño a la cabeza.
- **Dos armas en la mano:** siempre un arma de fuego y un bastón, nunca dos del mismo tipo. Se cambia con la rueda del mouse o Alt, y en mando con una flecha de la cruceta. Con el arma de fuego solo se puede lanzar el encantamiento; para usar los otros hechizos hay que cambiar al bastón. Con esto se resuelve el choque del clic derecho, y quedó explicado en la tabla de controles.
- **Encantamiento:** R o T, y en mando L2 + R2 a la vez.
- **Pasivas de aire:** siempre activas, sin ocupar ranura.
- **Escudo de hielo:** tiene QTE, que afecta su duración y su efectividad para bloquear.
- **Bastones:** se consiguen en cofres repartidos por el mapa.
- **Espada:** mango en 3D, hoja en pixel art y, por ahora, HUD medieval.
- **Boss final:** mezcla los dos estilos; cómo hacerlo está por definir.

**Preguntas que bloquean al arquitecto:**
1. **Espada elemental:** si solo hay dos ranuras (arma de fuego y bastón), ¿dónde va? ¿Reemplaza al bastón, al arma, o es una tercera ranura?
2. **Recarga y munición:** ¿las armas tienen cargador y se recargan? Si la recarga va en la R, el encantamiento queda en la T. ¿La munición es limitada? ¿De dónde sale?
3. **Resto de controles:** saltar, dash, granada, uso rápido de pociones o inyección, interactuar (cofres, portales), inventario y árboles. En mando, ¿R2 dispara y L2 apunta? ¿Qué flecha cambia de arma?
4. **Vida y maná:** ¿se regeneran solos o solo con pociones e inyecciones? ¿Hay maná en el futuro?
5. **Muerte:** ¿qué pasa cuando el jugador muere? ¿Vuelve a un checkpoint, reinicia la oleada o reinicia la zona?

**Pueden esperar:**
6. ¿Un solo fondo de skill points para los dos árboles, o puntos separados?
7. ¿Con qué empieza el jugador (arma, bastón, hechizos)? ¿Los demás hechizos se desbloquean en el árbol o se encuentran?
8. ¿Cuántos bastones hay? ¿El ataque de cada uno tiene elemento?
9. Además de bastones, ¿qué más traen los cofres?
10. ¿Cuánto debería durar una partida (15 o 30 minutos) y qué dificultad buscamos?

El resto está en la sección 17 del documento: subjefes, zonas bloqueadas, enemigos, objetos de misión, QTE, armaduras y nombre.

La granada sería compartiría con uso rápido junto con la poción. El jugador tendría que cambiarlo con la cruceta. O con shift. Interactuar sería con Y. O con F. Y el mando, en cuanto las armas de fuego, pues como en cualquier shooter. Sí, se regeneran solos también. Y por supuesto que hay maná en el futuro. ¿Cómo habría de no haber? El jugador empieza con bastón y hechizos. El jugador va a empezar en el castillo medieval. Va a matar un pequeño grupo de orcos. Entonces ahí va a interactuar con un objeto, va a pasar la primera cinemática sencilla, va a aparecer en el futuro. En el futuro va a pelear contra orcos armados . content.text:
Actualicé [Design/GDD.md](Design/GDD.md) a la **v0.5** y lo commiteé (`4b44ff0`).

**Qué incorporé:**
- **Sección 0, "Baseline":** el juego es un RPG clásico más un shooter clásico en primera persona. Todo lo que el documento no especifica se comporta como el jugador espera de esos géneros. Así el arquitecto no pregunta lo básico.
- **Espada:** es una tercera ranura especial.
- **Armas de fuego:** tienen cargador y se recargan con la R. La munición es limitada y la sueltan los enemigos.
- **Vida, maná y época:** vida y maná se regeneran solos y no hay estamina. Al cambiar de época se conserva todo.
- **Muerte, progreso y dificultad:** al morir se vuelve al último checkpoint. Hay un solo fondo de skill points para los dos árboles. Por ahora solo hay dificultad difícil, sin duración objetivo.
- **Controles:**
  - saltar con barra espaciadora o X;
  - dash con Ctrl o círculo;
  - interactuar con F o triángulo;
  - recargar con R;
  - encantamiento con T, porque la R queda para recargar;
  - la granada, la poción y la inyección comparten la ranura de uso rápido, que se rota con Shift o la cruceta.
- **Secuencia inicial:** castillo, grupo de orcos, objeto, cinemática 1, futuro, orcos armados, cinemática 2.
- **Cofres:** pueden dar armaduras, aunque es raro.

**Preguntas que bloquean al arquitecto:**
1. **Choque en el mando con un arma de fuego:** lo estándar es L2 para apuntar y R2 para disparar, pero L2 + R2 es el encantamiento. Apuntar y disparar a la vez lanzaría el encantamiento. Propongo que, con un arma de fuego en la mano, el encantamiento vaya en L1, que en ese momento está libre porque no se pueden lanzar hechizos. ¿Te sirve?
2. **Usar el objeto rápido:** Shift o la cruceta lo rotan, pero ¿con qué tecla se usa? ¿G, Q, R1?
3. **Hechizos iniciales:** ¿con cuáles empieza el jugador? ¿El resto se desbloquea en el árbol, en cofres o con bosses?
4. **Orcos armados:** el orco es medieval y su arma es cyberpunk. ¿Es un orco en pixel art con un arma 3D, como el jugador?
5. **Primera arma de fuego:** ¿de dónde la saca el jugador? ¿La encuentra al llegar al futuro, se la suelta un orco armado o la recibe en una cinemática?

**Pueden esperar:**
6. **Historia:** ¿quién es el jugador, qué es el objeto del castillo, por qué viaja y qué muestran las cinemáticas?
7. **Checkpoints:** ¿automáticos o un objeto que el jugador activa?
8. **Munición:** ¿una sola para todas las armas o una por tipo?
9. **Correr:** ¿hay sprint o lo cubre la pasiva de velocidad?
10. **Armaduras:** ¿una ranura o varias? ¿Qué más modifican aparte de la ralentización?

El resto sigue en la sección 17: teclas de inventario y pausa, bastones, escudo, recompensa por combinar estilos, subjefes, zonas, enemigos, objetos de misión, detalles del QTE y nombre.

7	## Changelog
8	- v0.5 (2026-11-12): sword is a third slot; magazines, reload, limited ammo dropped by enemies; health and mana regenerate, no stamina; state carries across eras; checkpoints; one skill point pool; controls filled in; opening sequence; armor from chests; difficulty = hard only for now.

13	
14	## 0. Baseline
15	At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.
16	
17	## 1. One-line pitch
18	A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.
19	
20	Working title: **TBD**.
21	
22	## 2. Pillars
23	1. **Two eras, one fight.** Past = magic, pixel art. Future = guns, 3D cyberpunk. Both feed the same character.
24	2. **Combos over specialization.** Spells and guns can be used in both eras, and the game rewards combining them. Weapon and spell mechanics have synergies.
25	3. **Fast and dynamic combat:** spells, ranged spells, shooting, and melee once the elemental sword is unlocked.
26	4. **Magic feels crafted, not triggered:** casting uses a two-part slowed-time quick-time event that scales the spell (see §7).
27	
28	## 3. Art rule (never broken)
29	- **Everything medieval, wizards and magic is pixel art (2D).**
30	- **Everything cyberpunk and futuristic is 3D.**
31	- **The rule follows the object, not the era.** A 3D gun stays 3D in the past; a pixel-art fireball stays pixel art in the future.
32	- **The player is a medieval mage, so the player is always pixel art, hands included.** In first person, the hands are always pixel art, even when they hold a 3D gun.
33	- No exceptions.
34	
35	## 4. World and travel
36	- **One map, two times** (past and future). The player travels between them **only through predefined portals** placed on the map.
37	- **Era-gated zones:** some zones are reachable in one era and not in the other.
38	- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
39	- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
40	- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
41	
42	### Opening sequence
43	1. The player starts in the **medieval castle** (past) with a **staff and spells**.
44	2. Kills a **small group of orcs**.
45	3. **Interacts with an object** → **short, simple cutscene #1**.
46	4. Appears in the **future**.
47	5. Fights **armed orcs**.
48	6. **Short cutscene #2.**
49	7. Rest of the game: **TBD**.
50	- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).
51	
52	## 5. Player progression
53	- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
54	- Progression is through **skill trees**: one for spells and one for weapons (see §13 for their look).
55	  - **Spell tree:** upgrades spells.
56	  - **Weapon tree:** damage, fire rate, **recoil** (better aim), **damage by distance** (shotgun stronger up close, rifle stronger far away), **headshot damage**.
57	- **One shared pool of skill points** for both trees.
58	- **Skill points** are given at specific points, mainly for defeating enemies:
59	  - defeating each **sub-boss**;
60	  - defeating each **boss**;
61	  - **clearing a wave** of enemies.
62	
63	## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
64	Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.
65	
66	| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS) |
69	| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
70	| **Ice** | Ice shield (held block, like a first-person RPG shield, but with a cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
71	| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |
72	
73	### Spell loadout
74	- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
75	- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
76	- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
77	- Keys: see §9.
78	
79	### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
80	- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
81	- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
82	- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
83	- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
84	- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
85	- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
86	- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.
87	
88	### General
89	- Spells cost **mana**.
90	- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**
91	- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
92	- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.
93	
94	## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
95	**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).
96	
97	Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.
98	
99	### Flow
100	1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
101	2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
102	   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
103	   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
104	3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
105	   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
106	   - Gamepad: the right stick.
107	4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.
108	
109	### Grading and cost
110	- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
111	- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
112	- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.
113	
114	### What each part scales
115	| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| Fireball | Damage | Blast radius / range |
118	| Ice wall | Duration and wall health | Width and height |
119	| Ice shield | Duration and block effectiveness (which part scales which: **TBD**) | |
120	| Others | **TBD**, following the same idea: part 1 = strength, part 2 = size/area/range |
121	
122	### Requirements for the architect
123	- **Every spell parameter is data, not code**, and every one can be tagged as scaled by part 1, part 2, or neither. Each spell defines its own min/max per parameter.
124	- The **time-slow amount is configurable** and can be modified by gear (e.g. some armor). Armor/gear as a system is otherwise **TBD**.
125	
126	## 8. Weapons and items
127	
128	### Held slots
129	- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
130	- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
131	- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).
132	- Staff in hand: basic magic attack + the 5 spells + the enchant. Gun in hand: shoot + aim + reload + the enchant only.
133	
134	### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
135	- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
136	- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
137	- Staff list and what each basic attack does: **TBD**.
138	
139	### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
140	- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
141	- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
142	- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
143	- **Limited ammo**, picked up from the floor where enemies drop it.
144	- **Electric grenade** (throwable).
145	
146	### Armor
147	- Found in **chests**, rarely.
148	- Known effect: some armor changes the QTE time-slow amount (§7). Other stats, slots and how it is equipped: **TBD**.
149	
150	### Chests
151	- Contain **staffs**, and rarely **armor**. Other contents: **TBD**.
152	
153	### Melee
154	- **No melee before the elemental sword** (§11).
155	
156	### Consumables
157	| Item | Era | Effect |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| Health potion | Past | Heals a set amount **over time** |
160	| Mana potion | Past | Restores a set amount of mana **over time** |
161	| Electric grenade | Future | Throwable, electric damage |
162	| Health injection | Future | Heals **instantly**, but less than the potion |
163	
164	### Synergies
165	Weapon mechanics and spell mechanics combine. The weapon enchant (§6) is the first confirmed one. Other synergies (e.g. shooting through a fire wall, electric grenade on an ice floor) are **TBD**.
166	
167	## 9. Controls
168	
169	| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |
170	|---|---|---|
171	| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
172	| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
173	| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | **TBD** |
174	| Aim (gun in hand) | Right click | **TBD** |
175	| Spell slot 1 (staff in hand) | Right click | L1 / LB |
176	| Spell slots 2–5 (staff in hand) | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
177	| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |
178	| Weapon enchant (any held weapon) | T (R is reload) | L2 + R2 together (LT + RT) — see open question 1 |
179	| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad arrow (**TBD** which) |
180	| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |
181	| Dash | Ctrl | Circle (B) |
182	| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | **TBD** | **TBD** |
183	| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad |
184	| Interact (chests, portals, objects) | F | Triangle (Y) |
185	| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
186	| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
187	| Inventory, skill trees, pause | **TBD** | **TBD** |
188	
189	Gun controls on gamepad follow the standard shooter layout.
190	
191	Right click means "spell slot 1" with the staff and "aim" with a gun; the two never clash because spells cannot be cast with a gun in hand.
192	
193	## 10. Enemies and encounters
194	- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
195	- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
196	- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
197	- **The true final boss.**
198	- Known enemies: **orcs** (past) and **armed orcs** (future). Other types and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).
199	- Enemies **drop ammo** on the floor.
200	
201	### Death and difficulty
202	- On death the player **returns to the last checkpoint**.
203	- **Difficulty: hard**, the only one for now. A separate normal mode is possible later (for example, the spell QTE only in hard); out of scope until the owner says otherwise.
204	- No target length: we build as much as the time allows.
205	
206	## 11. Bosses and endgame
207	**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
208	- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
209	- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
210	- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**
211	
212	Rewards:
213	| Defeated in | Drops |
214	|---|---|
215	| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |

14	## 0. Baseline
15	At its core this is a **classic first-person RPG plus a classic first-person shooter**. Anything not stated here behaves as players expect from those two genres (magazines and reload, ammo pickups, standard shooter gamepad layout, etc.). This document only lists what is specific to our game.
16	
17	## 1. One-line pitch
18	A fast first-person **shooter/RPG hybrid**: the player, a medieval mage, jumps through fixed portals between a **pixel-art medieval past** full of magic and a **3D cyberpunk future** full of guns, on the same map in two times, and wins by **mixing spells and firearms** rather than sticking to one style.
19	
20	Working title: **TBD**.
21	
22	## 2. Pillars
23	1. **Two eras, one fight.** Past = magic, pixel art. Future = guns, 3D cyberpunk. Both feed the same character.
24	2. **Combos over specialization.** Spells and guns can be used in both eras, and the game rewards combining them. Weapon and spell mechanics have synergies.
25	3. **Fast and dynamic combat:** spells, ranged spells, shooting, and melee once the elemental sword is unlocked.
26	4. **Magic feels crafted, not triggered:** casting uses a two-part slowed-time quick-time event that scales the spell (see §7).
27	
28	## 3. Art rule (never broken)
29	- **Everything medieval, wizards and magic is pixel art (2D).**
30	- **Everything cyberpunk and futuristic is 3D.**
31	- **The rule follows the object, not the era.** A 3D gun stays 3D in the past; a pixel-art fireball stays pixel art in the future.
32	- **The player is a medieval mage, so the player is always pixel art, hands included.** In first person, the hands are always pixel art, even when they hold a 3D gun.
33	- No exceptions.
34	
35	## 4. World and travel
36	- **One map, two times** (past and future). The player travels between them **only through predefined portals** placed on the map.
37	- **Era-gated zones:** some zones are reachable in one era and not in the other.
38	- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
39	- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
40	- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
41	
42	### Opening sequence
43	1. The player starts in the **medieval castle** (past) with a **staff and spells**.
44	2. Kills a **small group of orcs**.
45	3. **Interacts with an object** → **short, simple cutscene #1**.
46	4. Appears in the **future**.
47	5. Fights **armed orcs**.
48	6. **Short cutscene #2.**
49	7. Rest of the game: **TBD**.
50	- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).
51	
52	## 5. Player progression
53	- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
54	- Progression is through **skill trees**: one for spells and one for weapons (see §13 for their look).
55	  - **Spell tree:** upgrades spells.
56	  - **Weapon tree:** damage, fire rate, **recoil** (better aim), **damage by distance** (shotgun stronger up close, rifle stronger far away), **headshot damage**.
57	- **One shared pool of skill points** for both trees.
58	- **Skill points** are given at specific points, mainly for defeating enemies:
59	  - defeating each **sub-boss**;
60	  - defeating each **boss**;
61	  - **clearing a wave** of enemies.
62	
63	## 6. Magic (4 elements + weapon enchant)
64	Each element has 3 entries. Air is passives only; the other three are active spells.
65	
66	| Element | 1 | 2 | 3 |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| **Fire** | Fireball (projectile) | Fire wall | Flamethrower (sustained DPS) |
69	| **Lightning** | Lightning bolt (projectile) | Lightning rune trap on the ground; triggers when an enemy walks over it | Static-electricity ball: moves and damages every enemy around it |
70	| **Ice** | Ice shield (held block, like a first-person RPG shield, but with a cooldown and limits) | Ice wall | Ice floor: slows enemies, light crowd control |
71	| **Air** (passives) | Double jump | Improved dash | Increased movement speed |
72	
73	### Spell loadout
74	- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
75	- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
76	- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
77	- Keys: see §9.
78	
79	### Weapon enchant (always equipped)
80	- A spell that **cannot be unequipped**.
81	- Animation: the **left hand draws a magic glyph over the weapon held in the right hand**.
82	- Effect: the weapon is **temporarily buffed with magic** of one element.
83	- **Element:** chosen by the player when equipping the spell.
84	- **Uses the QTE** like every other spell (§7).
85	- **Does not work on the elemental sword.**
86	- Duration, cost and exact buff per element: **TBD**.
87	
88	### General
89	- Spells cost **mana**.
90	- **Health and mana regenerate on their own** (potions and the injection speed it up). **No stamina.**
91	- Numbers for each spell (damage, cost, cooldowns, upgrade tiers): **TBD**, given later.
92	- The ice shield's exact limits (duration, damage absorbed, break behavior): **TBD**.
93	
94	## 7. Spell-casting quick-time event
95	**Status:** wanted for every spell, the enchant included; still a trial for the 4-day schedule, so it must be possible to switch it off (spells then cast at a fixed default strength).
96	
97	Purpose: make magic feel more elaborate than pulling a trigger.
98	
99	### Flow
100	1. Player casts. **Time slows** by about **90%** (world at ~10% speed). Inspired by the slowed time some games use while the player picks combat hacks.
101	2. **Part 1 — button sequence → POWER.** Random sequence.
102	   - Keyboard & mouse: movement keys (W, A, S, D).
103	   - Gamepad: the four face buttons (A/B/X/Y or Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle).
104	3. **Part 2 — gesture → REACH.**
105	   - Mouse: left-to-right, top-to-bottom, a circle, etc.
106	   - Gamepad: the right stick.
107	4. Spell fires with its parameters scaled by the two results; time returns to normal.
108	
109	### Grading and cost
110	- Each step counts on its own: every mistake lowers the result of its part.
111	- **The spell is cast if the player gets at least one step right.** It fails only if **every** step is missed.
112	- **Mana is always spent**, even when the spell fails.
113	
114	### What each part scales
115	| Spell | Part 1 (power) | Part 2 (reach) |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| Fireball | Damage | Blast radius / range |
118	| Ice wall | Duration and wall health | Width and height |
119	| Ice shield | Duration and block effectiveness (which part scales which: **TBD**) | |
120	| Others | **TBD**, following the same idea: part 1 = strength, part 2 = size/area/range |
121	
122	### Requirements for the architect
123	- **Every spell parameter is data, not code**, and every one can be tagged as scaled by part 1, part 2, or neither. Each spell defines its own min/max per parameter.
124	- The **time-slow amount is configurable** and can be modified by gear (e.g. some armor). Armor/gear as a system is otherwise **TBD**.
125	
126	## 8. Weapons and items
127	
128	### Held slots
129	- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
130	- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
131	- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).
132	- Staff in hand: basic magic attack + the 5 spells + the enchant. Gun in hand: shoot + aim + reload + the enchant only.
133	
134	### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
135	- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
136	- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
137	- Staff list and what each basic attack does: **TBD**.
138	
139	### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
140	- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
141	- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
142	- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
143	- **Limited ammo**, picked up from the floor where enemies drop it.
144	- **Electric grenade** (throwable).
145	
146	### Armor
147	- Found in **chests**, rarely.
148	- Known effect: some armor changes the QTE time-slow amount (§7). Other stats, slots and how it is equipped: **TBD**.
149	
150	### Chests
151	- Contain **staffs**, and rarely **armor**. Other contents: **TBD**.
152	
153	### Melee
154	- **No melee before the elemental sword** (§11).
155	
156	### Consumables
157	| Item | Era | Effect |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| Health potion | Past | Heals a set amount **over time** |
160	| Mana potion | Past | Restores a set amount of mana **over time** |
161	| Electric grenade | Future | Throwable, electric damage |
162	| Health injection | Future | Heals **instantly**, but less than the potion |
163	
164	### Synergies
165	Weapon mechanics and spell mechanics combine. The weapon enchant (§6) is the first confirmed one. Other synergies (e.g. shooting through a fire wall, electric grenade on an ice floor) are **TBD**.
166	
167	## 9. Controls
168	
169	| Action | Keyboard & mouse | Gamepad |
170	|---|---|---|
171	| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
172	| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
173	| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | **TBD** |
174	| Aim (gun in hand) | Right click | **TBD** |
175	| Spell slot 1 (staff in hand) | Right click | L1 / LB |
176	| Spell slots 2–5 (staff in hand) | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
177	| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |
178	| Weapon enchant (any held weapon) | T (R is reload) | L2 + R2 together (LT + RT) — see open question 1 |
179	| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad arrow (**TBD** which) |
180	| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |
181	| Dash | Ctrl | Circle (B) |
182	| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | **TBD** | **TBD** |
183	| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad |
184	| Interact (chests, portals, objects) | F | Triangle (Y) |
185	| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
186	| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
187	| Inventory, skill trees, pause | **TBD** | **TBD** |
188	
189	Gun controls on gamepad follow the standard shooter layout.
190	
191	Right click means "spell slot 1" with the staff and "aim" with a gun; the two never clash because spells cannot be cast with a gun in hand.
192	
193	## 10. Enemies and encounters
194	- **Enemy waves (hordes).** Clearing a wave gives skill points.
195	- **A couple of sub-bosses.**
196	- **Two bosses** (the Valkyrie in each era, §11).
197	- **The true final boss.**
198	- Known enemies: **orcs** (past) and **armed orcs** (future). Other types and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).
199	- Enemies **drop ammo** on the floor.
200	
201	### Death and difficulty
202	- On death the player **returns to the last checkpoint**.
203	- **Difficulty: hard**, the only one for now. A separate normal mode is possible later (for example, the spell QTE only in hard); out of scope until the owner says otherwise.
204	- No target length: we build as much as the time allows.
205	
206	## 11. Bosses and endgame
207	**The Valkyrie (two bosses, one in each era).**
208	- **Past:** trapped inside magic runes in the medieval castle.
209	- **Future:** trapped in a cryogenic tube.
210	- The player must **free her and defeat her in both eras.**
211	
212	Rewards:
213	| Defeated in | Drops |
214	|---|---|
215	| Past (castle) | **Elemental stones/gems** |

content.text:
Tienes razón con los orcos: fue un error de lectura mío. Lo dejé escrito sin ambigüedad en §3: cada personaje tiene el estilo del mundo al que pertenece. El orco del castillo es un orco clásico en pixel art y el del futuro es un orco sci-fi 3D muy acorazado; son enemigos distintos, no el mismo orco en dos estilos. En el documento no nombré Warhammer: en la bitácora pública evitamos marcas ajenas.

[Design/GDD.md](Design/GDD.md) ya está en la **v0.6** y commiteado.

**Qué incorporé:**
- **Historia:** el mago va al castillo por curiosidad y queda atrapado al llegar al sello. En el futuro oye la voz de una mujer que le pide ayuda, y eso lo motiva. Hay pocas cinemáticas y son cortas.
- **Secuencia inicial:** orcos pixel, el sello y la cinemática 1, luego el futuro y orcos 3D. Uno de ellos suelta la primera arma; al recogerla sale la cinemática 2, y sin recogerla no se avanza.
- **Hechizos iniciales:** bola de fuego en nivel muy inicial, relámpago en nivel inicial y muro de hielo.
- **Encantamiento:** solo con el arma de fuego en la mano. En mando va en L1; con el arma en la mano, L2 apunta y R2 dispara.
- **Teclas:** F usa el objeto rápido y G interactúa.
- **Munición:** cada arma tiene un número fijo de cargadores, como en Counter-Strike. Se repone completa al viajar de época y entre medias se recoge del suelo.
- **Resto:** checkpoints automáticos, sin sprint y una sola ranura de armadura completa.

**Un desliz que ya corregí:** al commitear un typo arrastré sin querer tus cambios sin commitear de `CLAUDE.md` y `PREJAM_PREP.md`. Deshice ese commit (era local, no estaba pusheado) y esos dos archivos vuelven a estar como los tenías. Nada está pusheado todavía.

**Preguntas que bloquean al arquitecto:**
1. **Los otros 6 hechizos** (muro de fuego, lanzallamas, runa, bola estática, escudo y suelo de hielo): ¿se desbloquean con skill points en el árbol, se encuentran en cofres o los dan los bosses?
2. **Pasivas de aire:** ¿están desde el inicio o se aprenden durante el juego? Por ejemplo, el doble salto más adelante.
3. **Las otras dos armas:** ¿de dónde salen la escopeta y el rifle? ¿La primera que suelta el orco es la pistola?
4. **Teclas que faltan.** Te propongo esto; confírmalo o cámbialo:
   - en mando, usar el objeto rápido con R1;
   - cambiar de arma con la flecha arriba y rotar el objeto rápido con izquierda y derecha;
   - inventario en Tab, árboles en K (o como pestaña del inventario) y pausa en Esc.

**Pueden esperar:**
5. ¿La voz de la mujer es la valquiria? Si la libera, ¿por qué luego tiene que pelear contra ella: está corrompida, es una prueba, un malentendido?
6. ¿Viajar de época también repone vida y maná, o solo la munición?

El resto sigue en la sección 17: bastones, partes del QTE del escudo, armaduras, recompensa por combinar, subjefes, zonas, enemigos, objetos de misión, detalles del QTE y nombre.

content: Los demás hechizos se van a aprender porque en el castillo medieval va a haber zonas un poco como elementales y después de enfrentar al desafío correspondiente, ya sea oleada, miniboss o boss, el jugador va a través de un cofre o a través de recoger un libro o algo similar va a adquirir como los conocimientos de ese elemento y va a desbloquear los otros dos hechizos que le faltan. Las pasivas de aire, el jugador las va a adquirir de la misma manera que va a aprender los demás hechizos, los otros elementos. La rifle y la escopeta, el jugador los conseguirá más adelante jugando. Los recogerá del suelo de un enemigo que se lo dropeará. Acepto tu sugerencia de las teclas que faltan. En cuanto a la historia, por ahora el boss final va a ser un ente que es una combinación de una inteligencia artificial apocalíptica y de un fantasma que representa enfermedades. En realidad la voz que escucha el jugador no es la de la Valquiria, es la de ese ente haciéndose pasar por la Valquiria y pidiendo ayuda. La Valquiria es alguien a quien el ente manipuló en el tiempo y no logró el cometido. Entonces quedó atrapada tanto en el pasado como en el futuro. El jugador va a derrotar a la Valquiria, va a juntar los elementos que necesita y va a abrir este portal. Que es lo que siempre ha querido este ente, que alguien que abra el portal y que vaya con un cuerpo físico que ella pueda poseer para poder salir. Entonces, digamos que el jugador sigue a la perfección el plan del boss final, simplemente que pues el jugador lo derrota. Viajar de época repone todo. Van a ser un poco como las hogueras de Dark Souls. ¿Qué otras preguntas importantes tienes?

content.content:
42:- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
46:### Story premise
50:- Cutscenes: **few and short**, each one written for its situation.
59:7. Rest of the game: **TBD**.
84:- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
85:- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall. The other spells: see open questions.
151:- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.

content.content:
- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.

- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).

### Story premise
- The player is a **mage** who travels to the castle out of **curiosity**: he had heard it was a mysterious place.
- On reaching the **seal** in the castle he is **trapped** and thrown into the future.
- In the future he hears **a woman's voice asking for help**. That voice is his reason to fix the problem.
- Cutscenes: **few and short**, each one written for its situation.

### Opening sequence
1. The player starts in the **medieval castle** (past) with a **staff and the starting spells** (§6).
2. Kills a **small group of pixel-art orcs**.
3. **Interacts with the seal** → **short cutscene #1** (trapped, sent forward in time).
4. Appears in the **future**.
5. Fights **3D armed orcs**. One of the first ones **drops the first gun**.
6. The player **picks up the gun** → **short cutscene #2**. The player **cannot progress** without picking it up.
7. Rest of the game: **TBD**.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
- **Ammo works like classic tactical shooters:** each gun has a fixed number of spare magazines, and each magazine a fixed number of bullets.
- **All ammo refills completely every time the player travels between eras.**
- Between refills, ammo is **picked up from the floor** where enemies drop it.
- Level design keeps ammo tight: never infinite, never starving.
- **Electric grenade** (throwable).

### Armor
| Move | W A S D | Left stick |
| Look | Mouse | Right stick |
| Primary attack (staff: basic magic attack; gun: shoot) | Left click | R2 / RT |
| Aim (gun in hand) | Right click | L2 / LT |
| Spell slot 1 (staff in hand) | Right click | L1 / LB |
| Spell slots 2–5 (staff in hand) | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |
| Weapon enchant (gun in hand only) | T (R is reload) | L1 / LB (free with a gun in hand) |
| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad arrow (**TBD** which) |
| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |
| Dash | Ctrl | Circle (B) |
| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | F | **TBD** |
| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad |
| Interact (chests, portals, objects) | G | Triangle (Y) |
| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
| Inventory, skill trees, pause | **TBD** | **TBD** |

Gun controls on gamepad follow the standard shooter layout.

Right click / L1 change meaning with the held weapon and never clash: staff = spell slot 1; gun = aim (right click) and enchant (L1). L2 means "spell modifier" with the staff and "aim" with a gun.

lines: # Game Design Document (working draft)
> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.6, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus five rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.7, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus six rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog

+- v0.7 (2026-11-12): full story (the entity, the false voice, the Valkyrie); elemental zones in the castle unlock the rest of each element; air passives learned the same way; shotgun and rifle dropped by enemies; era travel restores everything (bonfire-like); remaining keys confirmed.

- v0.6 (2026-11-12): art rule clarified for characters (style of the world they belong to); story premise; opening sequence with the first gun; starting spells; enchant only with a gun in hand; key changes (F quick-use, G interact, L1 enchant on gamepad); counter-style ammo refilled on era travel; automatic checkpoints; no sprint; one full-armor slot.

- v0.5 (2026-11-12): sword is a third slot; magazines, reload, limited ammo dropped by enemies; health and mana regenerate, no stamina; state carries across eras; checkpoints; one skill point pool; controls filled in; opening sequence; armor from chests; difficulty = hard only for now.

- v0.4 (2026-11-12): weapon skill tree contents; two held slots (one gun + one staff) and how to switch; no spells with a gun except the enchant; enchant key; air passives always on; ice shield QTE; staffs from chests; sword blade is pixel art with a medieval HUD; final boss mixes both styles.
- **Cross-era unlocks:** some zones must be unlocked in the past so they open in the future (cause in the past, effect in the future).
- These interactions are few (short jam) but they exist and are part of level design.
- **Nothing is lost when changing era.** Health, mana, ammo, inventory, spells and weapons all carry over. Mana exists and works in the future; guns work in the past.
+- **Era travel restores everything** (health, mana, ammo), a bit like the rest points of classic action RPGs. Portals are the safe points of the map.
- A third, separate map unlocks late: a **dimension between space and time** where the true final boss lives (see §11).
-### Story premise
+### Story
- The player is a **mage** who travels to the castle out of **curiosity**: he had heard it was a mysterious place.
- On reaching the **seal** in the castle he is **trapped** and thrown into the future.
- In the future he hears **a woman's voice asking for help**. That voice is his reason to fix the problem.
+- **The twist:** the voice is **not the Valkyrie**. It is **the Entity**, the true final boss, pretending to be her.

+- **The Entity:** a fusion of an **apocalyptic artificial intelligence** and a **ghost that embodies disease**. It is locked in the dimension between space and time and wants out. To escape it needs two things: someone to **open the portal** and a **physical body to possess**.
+- **The Valkyrie:** someone the Entity **manipulated across time**. The plan failed, and she ended up **trapped in both eras** (runes in the past, cryogenic tube in the future).

+- **What the player does:** defeats the Valkyrie in both eras, gathers what is needed, and opens the portal: **exactly the Entity's plan**. The player walks in with the body it wants to possess. The only thing the Entity did not plan for: **the player beats it**.
- Cutscenes: **few and short**, each one written for its situation.
### Opening sequence
4. Appears in the **future**.
5. Fights **3D armed orcs**. One of the first ones **drops the first gun**.
6. The player **picks up the gun** → **short cutscene #2**. The player **cannot progress** without picking it up.
-7. Rest of the game: **TBD**.
+7. Rest of the game: elemental zones in the castle (§6), the two Valkyrie fights, the final portal (§11). Exact order and map flow: **TBD**.
## 5. Player progression
- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
### Spell loadout
- The player has **5 spells equipped** at a time and can **equip and unequip** them freely.
- **Air passives are always active**: they are not equipped and do not take a slot.
-- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall. The other spells: see open questions.
+- **Starting spells:** Fireball (very early tier), Lightning bolt (early tier), Ice wall.
+### Learning the other spells: elemental zones
+- The **medieval castle** has **elemental zones**, one per element.
+- Each zone has a **challenge**: a wave, a sub-boss or a boss.

+- After the challenge the player gets the element's **knowledge** (from a chest, a book or similar) and **unlocks the missing spells of that element** (fire: fire wall + flamethrower; lightning: rune trap + static ball; ice: ice shield + ice floor).
+- **Air passives** are learned the same way, in the air zone.
+- The spell tree then upgrades what the player knows.
- **Spells can only be cast with the staff in hand.** With a gun in hand, the only spell available is the weapon enchant. To cast, the player switches to the staff mid-fight.
- Keys: see §9.
### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)
- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
+- The **first gun** is dropped by one of the first armed orcs in the future (§4). The **shotgun and the rifle** are dropped later by enemies, picked up from the floor.
- With a gun in hand: **primary fire = shoot**, **secondary = aim**.
- **Magazines and reload**, like any shooter.
- **Ammo works like classic tactical shooters:** each gun has a fixed number of spare magazines, and each magazine a fixed number of bullets.
| Spell slots 2–5 (staff in hand) | 1, 2, 3, 4 | Hold L2 / LT + Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle (A, B, X, Y) |
| Reload (gun) | R | Standard shooter layout |
| Weapon enchant (gun in hand only) | T (R is reload) | L1 / LB (free with a gun in hand) |
-| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad arrow (**TBD** which) |
+| Switch staff ↔ gun (↔ sword) | Mouse wheel or Alt | D-pad up |
| Jump | Space | Cross (A) |
| Dash | Ctrl | Circle (B) |
-| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | F | **TBD** |
-| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad |
+| Quick-use item (grenade / potion / injection share one slot) | F | R1 / RB |
+| Cycle the quick-use item | Shift | D-pad left / right |
| Interact (chests, portals, objects) | G | Triangle (Y) |
| QTE part 1 | W A S D | Face buttons |
| QTE part 2 | Mouse gesture | Right stick |
-| Inventory, skill trees, pause | **TBD** | **TBD** |
+| Inventory | Tab | Options / View |
+| Skill trees | K (also a tab inside the inventory) | From the inventory |
+| Pause | Esc | Start / Menu |
Gun controls on gamepad follow the standard shooter layout.
- Art (§3): the **hilt is 3D** (it comes from the future), the **blade is pixel art** (it is magic).
- HUD: **medieval** (provisional).
- **Final portal:** combining the two quest items opens a portal to a separate map, a dimension between space and time, where the player fights the **true final boss**.
-- **True final boss:** a **mix of both art styles**. Undecided how: two phases with different styles, or one character in both styles at once, or something else (**TBD**).

+- **True final boss: the Entity** (story in §4). A **mix of both art styles**, which fits what it is (AI = 3D, ghost = pixel art). Undecided how: two phases with different styles, or one character in both styles at once, or something else (**TBD**).
- This happens in mid/late game.
## 12. Inventory

Answers get folded into the sections above as they come.

**Blocking (needed before the architect starts):**
1. **Enemy respawn:** like rest points in classic action RPGs, does era travel also **respawn the enemies**? Or do cleared areas stay cleared?
2. **Map flow:** what is the order after cutscene #2? Can the player pick the order of the elemental zones, or is it linear? Rough proposal to confirm or change: future intro → back to the castle → elemental zones (any order) → Valkyrie (past) → Valkyrie (future) → final portal.
3. **What the future has:** the elemental zones are in the castle. What does the player do in the future besides the intro and the Valkyrie (zones unlocked from the past, where the shotgun and rifle drop, sub-bosses)?
4. **Challenges per zone:** 4 elemental zones; which one ends in a wave, which in a sub-boss, which in a boss? Are the "couple of sub-bosses" the guardians of these zones?

**Can wait:**
5. **Valkyrie fight:** if she is a victim of the Entity, why does she fight the player (she thinks he serves the Entity, she is still under its control…)?
6. **Final boss mechanics:** does the possession attempt become part of the fight (e.g. a phase where it tries to take the player's body)?
7. **Staffs:** how many, and does each one's basic attack have an element?
8. **Ice shield QTE:** which part scales duration and which scales block effectiveness?
9. **Armor:** which stats besides the QTE time slow (defense, mana regen…)?
10. How "combining styles" is rewarded beyond synergies (combo meter, bonus damage, more skill points?).
11. Examples of era-gated zones and past→future unlocks.
12. Other enemy types per era.
13. The two quest items.
14. QTE: time limit, sequence length per spell, does the camera slow too.
15. Game and team name.
EOF

content.text:
Actualicé [Design/GDD.md](Design/GDD.md) a la **v0.7** y lo commiteé.

**Qué incorporé:**
- **Historia completa (§4):**
  - **El Ente:** es una IA apocalíptica fusionada con un fantasma de la enfermedad. Se hace pasar por la Valquiria para pedir ayuda.
  - **La Valquiria:** el Ente la manipuló a través del tiempo y, al fallar el plan, quedó atrapada en las dos épocas.
  - **El jugador:** cumple el plan del Ente al pie de la letra (abre el portal y llega con un cuerpo para poseer), pero lo derrota. Este giro también suma al "sello de autor".
- **Zonas elementales en el castillo:** cada una termina en un desafío (oleada, subjefe o jefe) y da el conocimiento del elemento con un cofre o un libro. Eso desbloquea los dos hechizos que faltaban de ese elemento. Las pasivas de aire se aprenden igual.
- **Armas:** la escopeta y el rifle los sueltan enemigos más adelante.
- **Viajar de época repone todo**, como una hoguera. Los portales funcionan como puntos seguros.
- **Teclas confirmadas:**
  - en mando, R1 usa el objeto rápido;
  - flecha arriba cambia de arma;
  - izquierda y derecha rotan el objeto rápido;
  - Tab abre el inventario, K los árboles y Esc la pausa.
- **Boss final:** sugerí que su mitad IA sea 3D y su mitad fantasma pixel art. Lo marqué como sugerencia, no como decisión.

**Preguntas importantes que quedan**, las que necesita el arquitecto para armar el mapa:
1. **Reaparición de enemigos:** como en las hogueras, ¿viajar de época también hace reaparecer a los enemigos? ¿O las zonas limpias se quedan limpias?
2. **Orden del juego tras la cinemática 2.** Te propongo esto para confirmar o cambiar: intro en el futuro, regreso al castillo, zonas elementales en el orden que elija el jugador, Valquiria del pasado, Valquiria del futuro y portal final.
3. **Qué hay en el futuro:** las zonas elementales están en el castillo. Además de la intro y la Valquiria, ¿qué hace el jugador en el futuro? Por ejemplo, zonas que se abren desde el pasado, dónde caen la escopeta y el rifle, o subjefes.
4. **Desafío de cada zona:** hay 4 zonas elementales. ¿Cuál termina en oleada, cuál en subjefe y cuál en jefe? ¿El "par de subjefes" son los guardianes de estas zonas?

**Pueden esperar:**
5. Si la Valquiria es víctima del Ente, ¿por qué pelea contra el jugador? ¿Cree que él sirve al Ente, o sigue bajo su control?
6. ¿El intento de posesión es parte de la pelea final? Por ejemplo, una fase en la que el Ente intenta tomar el cuerpo del jugador.

El resto sigue en la sección 17: bastones, QTE del escudo, armaduras, recompensa por combinar, enemigos, objetos de misión, detalles del QTE y nombre.

lines: # Game Design Document (working draft)
> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.7, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus six rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.8, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus seven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog
+- v0.8 (2026-11-12): enemies do not respawn; provisional game order; story questions parked; open questions narrowed to what the prototype and base systems need.

- v0.7 (2026-11-12): full story (the entity, the false voice, the Valkyrie); elemental zones in the castle unlock the rest of each element; air passives learned the same way; shotgun and rifle dropped by enemies; era travel restores everything (bonfire-like); remaining keys confirmed.

- v0.6 (2026-11-12): art rule clarified for characters (style of the world they belong to); story premise; opening sequence with the first gun; starting spells; enchant only with a gun in hand; key changes (F quick-use, G interact, L1 enchant on gamepad); counter-style ammo refilled on era travel; automatic checkpoints; no sprint; one full-armor slot.

- v0.5 (2026-11-12): sword is a third slot; magazines, reload, limited ammo dropped by enemies; health and mana regenerate, no stamina; state carries across eras; checkpoints; one skill point pool; controls filled in; opening sequence; armor from chests; difficulty = hard only for now.
4. Appears in the **future**.
5. Fights **3D armed orcs**. One of the first ones **drops the first gun**.
6. The player **picks up the gun** → **short cutscene #2**. The player **cannot progress** without picking it up.
-7. Rest of the game: elemental zones in the castle (§6), the two Valkyrie fights, the final portal (§11). Exact order and map flow: **TBD**.
+7. Back to the **castle**.
+8. **Elemental zones**, in the order the player chooses (§6).
+9. **Valkyrie, past.**
+10. **Valkyrie, future.**
+11. **Final portal** → the Entity (§11).
+Steps 7–11 are **provisional** (owner, 2026-11-12).
## 5. Player progression
- **No character levels / no XP leveling.**
- **The true final boss.**
- Known enemies: **orcs** (past) and **armed orcs** (future). Other types and behavior: **TBD**. Their art follows §3 (medieval = pixel art, cyberpunk = 3D).
- Enemies **drop ammo** on the floor.
+- **Enemies do not respawn.** A cleared zone stays cleared, also after era travel.
### Death and difficulty
- On death the player **returns to the last checkpoint**. Checkpoints are **automatic**.

- Examples of era-gated zones and past→future unlocks.

- Game and team name.
